highlights:

FIFA World Cup 202
[...]
## After having to watch the recent World Cup and European Championship on TV screens, Norway blazed through the qualifying tournament and beat former champion Italy home and away.
[...]
Norway enters the World Cup as an unproven entity. Despite having some big names in its ranks, Norway’s 28-year absence from the biggest stage leaves nothing to judge upon except recent results. For context, 16 players in the 26-man squad were not even born the last time the nation played in 1998.
[...]
But a stellar qualification campaign will make sure that no opponent will take the Nordic nation lightly. After having to watch the recent World Cup and European Championship on TV screens, Norway blazed through the qualifying tournament, scoring 37 goals and conceding just five, while also beating former champion Italy home and away.
[...]
Sixteen of those goals were bagged by the nation’s all-time top scorer Erling Haaland, who will be itching to find the back of the net in his first major tournament appearance in national colours.
[...]
While Haaland and Sorloth are heavily reliant on brute force and strength, RB Leipzig’s winger Antonio Nusa will hope to bring some flair to the team. The 20-year-old’s quick feet fuel his willingness to take on defenders, and he will be expecting to have a breakout campaign.
[...]
Its defence is boosted by the presence of Kristoffer Ajer and Julian Ryerson, with the latter having the ability to also occasionally chip in in the attack as an extra man on the right wing.Additionally, setpieces might be a weapon for the Nordic nation as it shares the tallest team title at this World Cup with Bosnia and Herzegovina, with an average squad height of 187.23 cm.
[...]
High-profile departures and missing out on a league title late might have overshadowed Erling Haaland’s season. But the Norwegian was in fine form again, grabbing his third Premier League Golden Boot (27 goals) in four years at the club and will be eager to extend his lead as Norway’s all-time top scorer.
[...]
After being part of the last Norway squad to play at the World Cup, Stale Solbakken was appointed as the nation’s head coach in 2020. His journey has had its ups and downs, including failing to qualify for the World Cup 2022 and Euro 2024. However, he found a pragmatic way of focusing play on his best players for success while also ensuring that a team-first approach exists in the squad.
[...]
##### Predicted XI (4-4-2)
[...]
Ørjan Nyland (gk), Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Wolfe, Martin Ødegaard, Sander Berge, Fredrik Aursnes, Antonio Nusa, Erling Haaland, Alexander Sørloth.

It’s 28 years since Norway last played at a men’s FIFA World Cup. Despite such a long hiatus, there’s a sense they could be back with a bang this summer.

The 2026 World Cup will be Norway’s first major men’s tournament since Euro 2000, and only their fifth appearance ever at either the World Cup for European Championship. They will first have the chance of showing such qualities against Iraq and Senegal at the World Cup, presumably hoping to have progress to the knockouts wrapped up after those two games.
[...]
On paper, their third match has the potential to be one of the most exciting games of the group stage as they tussle with France, currently ranked top of the FIFA world rankings. During Norway’s last World Cup appearance in 1998, they stunned a Brazil side who were the top-ranked side at the time, winning 2-1 in the group only to be eliminated in the last 16 by Italy. As a result, Norway have never won a knockout match in a major tournament.
[...]
But it feels highly probable that run will end this summer.
[...]
In a way, though, it’s a shame from an entertainment perspective that their encounter with France isn’t earlier than Matchday 3 because, in this expanded tournament that features a round of 32, there is likely to be less jeopardy than prior tournaments in the group stage.
[...]
Meeting France on MD1 or MD2 would likely have more riding on it that on MD3. Nevertheless, it’s still a fixture that allows them the opportunity to make something of a statement. Even if it’s ultimately against an under-strength France, it could provide a timely confidence boost.
[...]
The aim, then, must be for Norway to earn a first ever knockout win at a World Cup as a minimum. If they get that far, they have the talent to beat anyone they face in a one-off match.
[...]
Norway head into the 2026 World Cup with the greatest generation of players they’ve ever had; if they can live with such expectation, there’s no reason why this can’t be a tournament to remember for Haaland and Co.
